approach: Count the rejected, failed or timed-out jobs in one retry lineage (a chain of "try again on <job>" requests) from the job records. The count is built on `job_history` and `retries_by_job` in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs`, with a named constant `LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 3`. A new `lineage_stop` returns None when the job is in no lineage or has fewer than 3 failed attempts. Otherwise it returns the failed job ids, the findings seen in at least two attempts, a ready-to-queue narrower request built with `StewardRequest::new`, and any narrower request already queued for that lineage. The drain asks this through two new `Steps` methods with defaults, so no existing implementor changes. The drain asks at TWO places in `Drain::attempts`. (a) Right after each failed attempt, before the `failures >= ATTEMPTS` return and before the loop goes back to dispatch a retry. This catches a lineage that reaches 3 on the item's second in-run attempt, which today ends as `Failed` (drain.rs:1941-1955), and it stops the in-item 4th retry. (b) At the loop top before a non-landing attempt, for a queued "try again on <job>" item whose chain already holds 3 failures. At the limit the drain dispatches nothing more, queues the narrower request once through `Athena::queue` (marker line `Lineage <root>` makes queuing idempotent), and ends the item with a new `ItemEnd::LineageStopped`, which `finish` passes over with the reason. A hand `athena retry` stays unlimited. A new `lineage-limit` default is added to `defaults.toml`. The reader's token budget leaves no room for it, so the plan splits `buy-first` (and `lazy-requests` only if still over) at their real sentence break, and updates the `budget reader` line in `docs/system-facts.md`, which is what that file says to do. The fixtures are rebuilt so the drain's next attempt would really be the 4th, and each stop path has a test that fails without it.

decisions.choice: Ask `Steps::lineage_stop` at two points in `Drain::attempts` (drain.rs:1855-1957) through one helper `lineage_end(item, job) -> Option<ItemEnd>`. Point 1: in the `if passed.is_none()` block, after the `paused_reason` check and before `run_job`, with `last_job` (covers a queued retry item already over the limit, and an interrupted item). Point 2: right after `failures += 1`, only when `passed.is_none()` and `paused_reason(item)` is None, and BEFORE the `failures >= ATTEMPTS` return (covers the lineage reaching 3 on the item's own second attempt, and stops the in-item `ReadOf::Retry(last_job)` 4th attempt at once). The helper calls `lineage_stop`, then `queue_narrower`, writes one `drain      <item> stopped: ...` UI line plus a `note_once`, and returns `ItemEnd::LineageStopped(reason)`.
decisions.reason: One loop pass is one `run_job` (read and run, drain.rs:1529-1706). After a failure the function either returns at `failures >= ATTEMPTS` or loops back to read a retry of `last_job`. A check at the loop top alone never sees a lineage that became 3 on the last in-run attempt: it returned `Failed` with no narrower request and no recorded findings. A check after the failure alone would miss a queued item whose chain is already at 3 before its first read. Pause keeps priority (a paused line returns `ItemEnd::Paused` as today), so the scope guard's own stop is unchanged. A landing retry of a passed job (`passed.is_some()`) is not a new attempt and is not checked. `last_job` is updated to the failed job when `read` is true (drain.rs:1920-1923), so the lineage is measured from the attempt just made.

rejected.option: Check only at the loop top
rejected.why: Misses the lineage that reaches 3 on the item's second in-run attempt: it returns `ItemEnd::Failed` first (critic finding 2).
It would also block the operator's own `athena retry`, the manual override, and the drain would see an error rather than a stop it could answer with a narrower request.

decisions.choice: `lineage_attempts(records, job)` in retry.rs calls `job_history` ONCE, derives the forward map with a private `retries_in(records, &history)` that `retries_by_job` is changed to call (same result), and returns early (empty) when the given job has no `retry_of` and no entry in the forward map. Otherwise it walks forward to the newest standing retry, then back along `retry_of`, with a seen-set and `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` each way, and keeps jobs whose `records.jobs[id].state()` is Closed(Rejected | Failed | TimedOut), oldest first. `pub const LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT: usize = 3`.
decisions.reason: Reuses the one place the "try again on" form is read (`retried_job`). One `job_history` pass per call, and no further work for a job in no lineage (critic finding 4). Counts hand and drain retries alike. `retries_by_job` already skips unrun retries (dropped, declined, abandoned, stale, closed). `job_history` maps Stale to Failed, so state is read from the record to keep stale out. TimedOut counts because `athena retry` and `RunStep::Failed.retry` (drain.rs:1696-1701) treat it like rejected or failed. The walk back starts at the given job whether or not it is itself failed, so an unrun queued item `try again on <j3>` counts j3 and its ancestors.

Then the verifier runs the budgets test to show the reader set equals the updated facts line.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs `mod tests` (helpers `records_with` ~1773, `outcome` ~1754, `finding` ~3113, `two_majors_and_a_minor` ~3230) build in-memory `Records` with a chain j1 <- j2 <- j3 of "try again on" requests. They assert: `LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT == 3`; `lineage_attempts` returns the failed ids oldest first when called from any job of the chain and from an unrun queued item that retries j3; a landed job, a dropped or stale retry, and a job in another lineage are not counted; rejected, failed and timed-out each count; a job in no lineage returns empty; a cyclic request does not loop; `retries_by_job` returns the same map as before for the same records.
demonstrations.observes: The tests pass: the constant is 3, and the count over the `job_history`/`retries_by_job` chain matches the records for each shape.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the helper the test module does not compile. With a counting bug (stale counted, forward walk missing, queued item not walking back) one of the shape assertions fails.

demonstrations.method: Two tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, both over `drain::drain(&real_steps(&athena, &lander), limits, &Quiet)` with a `Scenario` whose verdict is `fail` with every criterion met and one major finding `the description lists no callers` (judge: a Fail verdict or a blocker/major finding gives final_verdict Fail, verify.rs:649-672; no unmet criterion, so the scope guard's T4 does not pause the line). Test `a_lineage_with_three_rejected_attempts_gets_no_fourth_attempt` (in-item path): queue FIRST; run it by hand (`athena.go` until Finished) to a rejected j1; `athena.retry(j1)` and run that proposal to a rejected j2; `athena.queue("try again on <j2>")` = q. Keep `scenario.invocations` before `script()`. Drain with `max_jobs: 1`. The drain reads and runs q (the 3rd failure); before it can read a retry of q it stops. Assert: j1, j2 and q are all `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Rejected)`; `lineage_attempts(&records, q).len() == 3`; no request job in the records has text `try again on <q>`; Producer invocations grew by exactly 1 over the drain; the lander landed nothing; `steps.paused(&[q])` is empty (so the lineage rule, not the scope guard, ended the item); the `plan       <q> passed over:` UI line names the lineage stop (use `Lines` as the test at 5549 does). Test `a_queued_retry_of_a_lineage_with_three_failures_is_not_read_or_run` (loop-top path): hand-reject j1, j2 (`athena.retry`) and j3 (`athena.retry(j2)`), then `athena.queue("try again on <j3>")` = q; drain with `max_jobs: 1`. Assert: Producer and Verifier invocations unchanged by the drain (the planning pass may read q, so Reader count is not asserted); q is not Closed; no job has text `try again on <q>`; the passed-over line names the lineage.
demonstrations.observes: Exactly three rejected jobs in the lineage and none is a retry of the third; the drain starts one job, not two; the output says the lineage was stopped. The sibling command `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain a_queued_retry_of_a_lineage_with_three_failures_is_not_read_or_run` shows a queued 4th is not dispatched either.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check after a failure, the loop goes back and reads `ReadOf::Retry(q)`, which makes a job `try again on <q>` and runs it: the no-retry-of-q assertion, the count-equals-3 assertion and the Producer-delta-of-1 assertion fail. Without the loop-top check, the queued-retry test runs q (a Producer invocation appears and q closes), so it fails. (Critic finding 1: the lineage is built so the drain's next attempt would be the 4th, so the test fails without the gate.)
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `drain::drain` over `RealSteps` (exists; `real_steps` at tests/drain.rs:4365, `work_everything` at 4392, `Lines` UI and `RecordingLander` used throughout). The fake agent comes from `Fixture::athena(Scenario.script())` (tests/common/mod.rs, exists) and only plays the rejecting verifier; it holds no limit logic. Hand attempts go through `Athena::go` and `Athena::retry` (exist; tests/retry.rs:181 and tests/drain.rs:5108 show the use). The all-met-plus-major verdict helper is added by plan step 11. The `Steps` methods, `ItemEnd::LineageStopped` and both checks are added by plan steps 4 to 6.

demonstrations.method: Three tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs. (a) `the_lineage_stop_queues_one_narrower_request_that_carries_the_repeated_findings`, on the in-item fixture of criterion 3 (after the drain with `max_jobs: 1`): load `Records`, select requests whose text contains the marker `Lineage <j1>`; assert exactly one, on channel `cli`, text not starting with `try again on`, containing `the description lists no callers` (it repeated in j1, j2 and q), the three failed job ids, and `request_text_acceptance(&text)` non-empty. Then call `steps.lineage_stop(q)` and `steps.queue_narrower(&stop)` on the same `RealSteps` and assert the returned id equals the queued one and `fx.head()` is unchanged (no second request). Then drain again and assert the marker count is still 1. (b) `a_lineage_that_reaches_three_failures_on_the_items_second_attempt_queues_the_narrower_request`: hand-reject j1, then `athena.queue("try again on <j1>")` = q; drain with `max_jobs: 2`. The drain runs q (2nd failure of the lineage), retries as r (3rd), and with the check after the failure stops before the `failures >= ATTEMPTS` return. Assert: exactly one marker request exists; the display output does not contain `failed twice`; no job retries r; the passed-over line names the lineage. (c) core unit tests in reading.rs for finding selection: a finding in 2 of 3 attempts is listed, one in 1 is not, the `none repeated` wording, the request builds with `StewardRequest::new` and its text is accepted by `request_text_acceptance`/`request_text_touches`, and the marker lookup finds the queued request.
demonstrations.observes: One narrower request carries the repeated finding; a second queue call and a second drain add none. The sibling command `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain a_lineage_that_reaches_three_failures_on_the_items_second_attempt_queues_the_narrower_request` shows the request is queued even when the 3rd failure is the item's last in-run attempt.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without queuing, no request carries the marker and the count of 1 fails. Without the marker lookup, the second queue call writes a second request and the unchanged-head assertion fails. If findings were not carried, the text assertion fails. Without the check after a failure (only the loop-top check), test (b) ends `ItemEnd::Failed` with no marker request and the display says `failed twice`, so it fails (critic finding 2).
demonstrations.seam: `RealSteps::lineage_stop` and `RealSteps::queue_narrower` (added by plan steps 4 and 5) over a real `Athena` and fixture repository (exists); the stop and request text come from `athena_core::reading::lineage_stop` (plan step 2) computed from the fixture's own records. The fake agent only plays the rejecting verifier. Nothing under test sits in a double.

open_questions: User: should a hand-run `athena retry` also stop at 3 failed attempts? The plan limits only the drain and keeps the manual command as the operator's override, because the request says Athena should stop retrying.
User: is counting a timed-out job as a failed attempt acceptable? The request says "rejected or failed"; the plan also counts timed-out, since `athena retry` and the drain treat the three alike.

User: may the producer edit the `budget reader` line in docs/system-facts.md and the matching prose row in docs/design/context-engineer.md? Neither is a listed deliverable, but any added default changes the computed reader size and the budgets test compares that line exactly. The plan assumes yes and trims as little as possible from `buy-first` and, only if needed, `lazy-requests`.
